figures.caption: FIGURE 1: Three core methodological perspectives con- nected in this survey: spatio-temporal graph modeling, un- certainty quantification, and explanation diagnostics. The RER framework additionally evaluates temporal integrity, robustness, statistical comparison, scope, computational ac- countability, and reproducibility.

FIGURE 2: High-level pipeline of a GNN-based forecasting system with integrated reliability analysis. Multivariate time series are mapped to a graph, processed by a spatio-temporal model, and evaluated or equipped with uncertainty and ex- planation mechanisms.
FIGURE 3: Reference spatial topology for METR-LA. The physical road-network adjacency is used as the benchmark graph context for the primary dataset.

FIGURE 4: Cross-dataset MAE comparison across all seven models. Under the archived model-specific configurations, D2STGNN attains the lowest MAE on METR-LA and PEMS-BAY, whereas STAEformer attains the lowest MAE on PEMS04. Bars show mean MAE over seeds 43–45; error bars denote sample standard deviation; ⋆marks the lowest mean MAE within each dataset.

FIGURE 5: Empirical coverage by forecast horizon for pooled and per-horizon normalized ensemble-conformal calibration at a nominal 90% level. Per-horizon calibration reduces the horizon-dependent under- and overcoverage observed with pooled calibration.

FIGURE 6: Cross-dataset normalized ensemble-conformal results computed from the retained member predictions. Empirical marginal coverage remains near the 90% target for both variants. Ensemble composition differs across datasets, so the comparison concerns the complete pipelines, not individual backbones.

FIGURE 7: Checkpoint versus mask main-effect SD for the 3 × 5 crossed design: D2STGNN and STID on all three datasets and MegaCRN on METR-LA, at both ablation rates (14 cells). Points above the equality line indicate greater checkpoint variability; points below indicate greater mask variability.

FIGURE 8: Degree-matched control for top-10 sensor zero-ablation, 7 model/dataset cases, 30 random draws per control. Error bars show ±1 SD across the 30 draws. Structural GNNExplainer rankings are used for D2STGNN and MTGNN; STID uses the explicitly non-structural proxy ranking. The selected sensor set does not clearly separate from either control in most cases; STID/PEMS04 shows the most extreme reversal observed under this diagnostic (the selected sensors change test MAE less than almost every random or degree-matched draw).

FIGURE 9: Sensor-ranking deletion-fidelity summary. The right panel presents the all-model METR-LA diagnostic at k = 10, while the left panel summarizes cross-dataset behavior for the subset with transfer checks. Rankings are structural GNNExplainer diagnostics for graph-dependent models and proxy-derived diagnostics for STID and STNorm; structural GNNExplainer is N/A for the latter configurations.

FIGURE 10: Cross-method sensor-ranking agreement on METR-LA. Integrated Gradients is compared with structural GNNExplainer for graph-dependent models and with the explicitly non-structural proxy ranking for STID and STNorm. The low top-10 overlap indicates substantial method dependence in the selected sensor sets under this diagnostic.
FIGURE A.1: Supplementary horizon-wise MAE profiles at H3, H6, and H12 across the three datasets.

FIGURE A.2: METR-LA per-horizon normalized ensemble-conformal behavior for the six-architecture ensemble. Empirical marginal coverage remains near the 90% target while interval width grows with forecast horizon; Figure 5 extends this view to all three datasets.

FIGURE A.3: Coverage–width trade-off for fixed and per-horizon normalized ensemble-conformal prediction. Ensemble composition differs across datasets. Comparisons between correction variants are most interpretable within each dataset.
FIGURE A.4: Per-horizon interval widths from the fixed and per-horizon conformal metric artifacts.
FIGURE A.5: Per-horizon empirical marginal coverage from the conformal metric artifacts compared with the nominal 90% target.
FIGURE A.6: Illustrative single-window forecast with fixed versus per-horizon conformal intervals on METR-LA.
FIGURE A.7: MC Dropout predictive variance and empirical coverage on METR-LA for the seven evaluated architecture– configuration pairs using 50 stochastic forward passes.

FIGURE A.8: Sensor-ranking fidelity ratio as a function of the sensor zero-ablation budget on METR-LA. Rankings are aggregated from GNNExplainer edge scores for graph-dependent models and are proxy-derived for STID and STNorm; structural GNNExplainer is N/A for the latter configurations.

FIGURE A.9: MAE change under selected-sensor versus random-sensor zero ablation on METR-LA. Rankings are derived from GNNExplainer edge-mask scores for graph-dependent models and from the explicitly non-structural proxy diagnostic for STID.

FIGURE A.10: Detailed METR-LA perturbation-stability heatmap for the top-10 sensor rankings. Rankings are structural GNNExplainer diagnostics for graph-dependent models and proxy-derived diagnostics for STID and STNorm.
FIGURE A.11: Raw top-10 Integrated Gradients sensors per model on METR-LA.
FIGURE A.12: Cross-model consensus of Integrated Gradients top-10 sensors on METR-LA.
FIGURE A.13: Additional XAI results for attention entropy and cross-dataset fidelity transfer.
FIGURE A.13: Additional XAI results for attention entropy and cross-dataset fidelity transfer.
